title: Why are Java Streams called lazy, and how do intermediate vs terminal operations, short-circuiting, and fused operations exploit laziness?
keyPoints: Intermediate operations are lazy: they register a pipeline stage but execute nothing until a terminal operation triggers them.
Terminal operations are eager: they trigger the entire pipeline and produce a result or side effect.
Short-circuit intermediates (limit, takeWhile) truncate the stream; short-circuit terminals (findFirst, anyMatch) stop processing entirely.
Loop fusion means multiple operations execute in a single pass per element, not one pass per operation.
Without a terminal operation, the entire pipeline is dead code: filter, map, and sorted never execute.
Combining laziness, fusion, and short-circuit means 10 million elements with limit(3) may process only a handful.
A pipeline with only intermediate operations and no terminal compiles and runs but produces no output or side effects.

s1_definition.oneliner: Streams are lazy because intermediate operations build a pipeline description without executing, and only a terminal operation triggers processing, enabling short-circuit and fusion optimisations.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Lazy intermediates**: `filter`, `map`, `sorted`, `distinct`, `flatMap`, `limit`, `skip`, `peek` do nothing when called; they register stages.
- **Eager terminals**: `collect`, `forEach`, `reduce`, `count`, `findFirst`, `anyMatch` trigger execution.
- **Short-circuit intermediates**: `limit(n)` and `takeWhile(Predicate)` truncate the stream.
- **Short-circuit terminals**: `findFirst()`, `findAny()`, `anyMatch()`, `allMatch()`, `noneMatch()` stop processing early.
- **Loop fusion**: multiple stateless operations on the same element happen in one pass, not separate iterations.
- **Dead code**: a pipeline without a terminal never executes.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine filing complaints at National Bank of India. Form A (filter: is this valid?), Form B (map: assign case number), Form C (collect: file in records). Eager processing: the bank processes all 1,000 complaints through Form A first, then all through Form B, then all through Form C: three separate passes. Lazy processing: the bank picks up complaint number 1, runs it through A, B, C in one go, then picks up number 2. If the manager says "I only need the first valid complaint" (findFirst), the bank stops after processing just a few.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Lazy Pipeline (nothing executes until terminal):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  stream()     → descriptor created      (no execution)
  .filter()    → stage added to chain    (no execution)
  .map()       → stage added to chain    (no execution)
  .sorted()    → stage added to chain    (no execution)
  ─── nothing happens above ───
  .toList()    → TERMINAL: triggers everything!

  Short-circuit:
  ──────────────
  10,000,000 elements
       │
  .filter(...)          → checks one at a time
  .limit(3)             → STOPS after 3 pass through
       │
  Only ~handful processed out of 10 million!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Streams are lazy because intermediate operations do nothing when called. They only register stages in a pipeline descriptor. Execution begins only when a terminal operation triggers the pipeline. This laziness enables three optimisations: loop fusion processes each element through all stateless stages in a single pass, short-circuit operations stop early when the result is determined, and unnecessary work is eliminated.

The combination is powerful. For 10 million transactions with limit(3), only a handful of elements are pulled and processed, with zero intermediate collections created. Without a terminal operation, the entire pipeline is dead code.

In Rajesh's loan eligibility service at National Bank of India, findFirst for eligible customers processed only 2 of 8 customers: the first failed the credit check (dropped by filter), the second passed all checks (findFirst received the result and stopped). The remaining 6 customers were never evaluated.

Remember one sentence: intermediate operations are lazy descriptions, terminal operations trigger everything, and short-circuit stops the pipeline early.
